answer: A durable defence is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can trade, and misbehaviour burns part of that stake, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Reputation then accrues slowly, like an ember that needs steady tending rather than a zephyr of fresh accounts, and decays when an agent goes idle, so a Sybil swarm cannot buy trust overnight. Honest agents carve a lasting niche in the karst of the market, a slow and costly record that cheap copies cannot fake.
